experiments.name: cache_lookup
experiments.workload: InductorPass.hash_source repeated over 5 source objects, 10000 lookups/repeat, 5 repeats; per-call ms
experiments.note: base = recompute inspect.getsource+sha256 each call; gold = functools.cache wrapped (cold miss then hits); speedup = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios

reported.scope: ms per 'cache lookup' (PR body does not define granularity; likely per-uuid() computation -- inferred, not quoted)
reported.scale_note: SAME unit (ms) but NOT scale-comparable. Reported 32.5->11.3ms is the PR's 'cache lookup time' whose scope the PR body does NOT specify (inferred to be per full uuid() computation over the pass classes). Our bench = ms per SINGLE hash_source() call (total_ms/n_lookups over 5 objects), so ~92x smaller. Ratio also differs (measured 354x vs reported 2.88x): our gold is a pure functools.cache HIT (trivial) vs base paying getsource+sha256 every call; the PR's 2.88x is diluted because uuid() does other non-cached work. Direction genuine; absolute ms and ratio not 1:1.
